comment: ERROR AND MISSING are the two RECOVERY node types, and they were the last two html types in no classification bucket — which is why SPEC section A was red. They are read together on one line (`n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing`) because they are one event seen two ways: a region the parser could not read, and a token it inserted to keep going. MISSING is matched by the `isMissing` PROPERTY, not the type string, which is why a census looking only for type names did not find it. This fixture makes the classification load-bearing by pinning the three-part contract it claims: REPORT the broken node with its own line, BYPASS it (no symbol of its own), and KEEP PUBLISHING everything around it. A classification that said 'silent' would have been the convenient answer and would have been wrong — silence means 'correctly emits nothing', and this emits a diagnostic.  ON THE ERROR PIN: `expectErrors` compares EVERY key of an entry against the error, with no key filtering, so a `comment` inside one is compared as though it were an error field and the assertion can never match. The prose therefore lives in this top-level comment and the entries carry fields only. The pin is on STRUCTURE — the ERROR node's own span, line 7 columns 20-25, severity warning — rather than on a message phrase, which is what makes it survive a reworded message and fail on a moved span. An error reported at the document root, or at line 1, or at the enclosing element's start, is a diagnostic nobody can act on, and this is the assertion that would notice.

expectSymbols.name: error-recovery
expectSymbols.comment: the document module still publishes: a recovery region does not void the file

expectSymbols.name: around
expectSymbols.comment: the element CONTAINING the ERROR node is not itself an error — tree-sitter's ERROR wraps the unreadable text, not the enclosing element, and the analyzer reads the element normally

expectSymbols.name: after
expectSymbols.comment: elements AFTER the broken region are unaffected — the walk does not stop at the first error

expectSymbols.name: unterminated
expectSymbols.comment: an unterminated element still yields a symbol bounded by the recovery

expectRelationships.comment: containment survives the error: the broken node is bypassed, not propagated

a RESOURCE on an element the parser had to repair is still a real dependency. Suppressing it would make a malformed document look like a document with no dependencies, which is a data-loss failure wearing a syntax-error costume

forbidRelationships.comment: the ERROR node is BYPASSED, so it must not become a symbol and must not be named. An edge to the raw broken text (`<<<>>`) is the seam's own documented anti-pattern — the block's text is never a target, because the analyzer reads AST nodes and never source text.

expectErrorCount.comment: exactly two: the ERROR node itself, and the syntax error the engine reports for the same region. A >=1 assertion would be satisfied by either alone, and the PAIR is the contract — the analyzer's own report plus the engine's, for one broken region and not two.
